text: If two circles touch one another externally, (then) the (straight-line) joining their centers will go through the point of union. For let two circles, $ABC$ and $ADE$, touch one another externally at point $A$, and let the center $F$ of $ABC$ be found [Prop.~3.1], and (the center) $G$ of $ADE$ [Prop.~3.1]. I say that the straight-line joining $F$ to $G$ will go through the point of union at $A$.
For (if) not (then), if possible, let it go like $FCDG$ (in the figure),
assertion: the straight-line from F to G goes like FCDG (not through A)

frame.supposition: the straight-line joining $F$ to $G$ does not go through the point of union at $A$

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: let it go like $FCDG$ (in the figure)

text: Therefore, since point $F$ is the center of circle $ABC$, $FA$ is equal to $FC$.

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: point $F$ is the center of circle $ABC$

text: Again, since point $G$ is the center of circle $ADE$, $GA$ is equal to $GD$.

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: point $G$ is the center of circle $ADE$

text: And $FA$ was also shown (to be) equal to $FC$. Thus, the (straight-lines) $FA$ and $AG$ are equal to the (straight-lines) $FC$ and $GD$.

spans.label: assumption
spans.text: $FA$ was also shown (to be) equal to $FC$

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: $FA$ and $AG$ are equal to the (straight-lines) $FC$ and $GD$

text: So the whole of $FG$ is greater than $FA$ and $AG$.
assertion: FG is greater than FA + AG

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the whole of $FG$ is greater than $FA$ and $AG$

assertion: FG is also less than FA + AG (by triangle inequality)

text: Thus, the straight-line joining $F$ to $G$ cannot not go through the point of union at $A$.
assertion: the straight-line joining F to G does go through the point of union at A

frame.closes: the straight-line joining $F$ to $G$ does not go through the point of union at $A$

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: the straight-line joining $F$ to $G$ cannot not go through the point of union at $A$

assertion: the straight-line FG goes through point A

text: Thus, if two circles touch one another externally, (then) the [straight-line] joining their centers will go through the point of union. (Which is) the very thing it was required to show.
